answer: Before each crossing the guide probes the crevasses with a rope, and the survey log holds the probe, the crossing and the guide's signature. A saffron crossing claimed as probed fails the log: the rope must have sounded the ice at the mirror of the crossing, and a crossing never probed has no depth to report. Forging a season of crossings means bribing the guide, faking thirty surveys and paying 20,400, and the ledge log is read before every traverse, so a crossing whose probe was never signed is closed to the party.
